lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Past the ferry steps and a very suspicious seagull, a market stall leans on the quay. It hasn't sold a thing since a storm in 1998.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Ah, the harbor stall. I sold my first cherry tarts here, standing on an upturned crate because I was too short for the counter.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: The Harbor Festival is coming. The whole town turns up, hungry and loud. Whoever feeds them is remembered for a year.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: You'll want fruit, dear. Plenty of it. And a stall that doesn't try to eat your thumbs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A crate of berries has already been left on the counter. A note, unsigned: 'For the festival. P.S. The seagull is called Gerald.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman in a captain's cap strides down the gangway like she owns the sea. The ferry behind her seems to agree.

lines.speaker: marisol
lines.text: Captain Marisol. I run the ferry, and I've been stuck eating gas-station sandwiches for six years. This stall used to fix that.

lines.speaker: marisol
lines.text: Your gran's fruit tarts were the reason I took this route in the first place. Tell me you've kept the recipe.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: It's on the third page, Captain. We're nearly there.

lines.speaker: marisol
lines.text: Good. A captain on a full stomach is a patient captain. A captain on a gas-station sandwich is a threat to navigation.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A big man with a bigger beard wrestles a tray of mackerel across the quay and parks it by the stall. Several gulls take an interest.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: Pell. Fishmonger. Don't mind the smell. It's mostly honest.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: I'd like a scone. Plain. Warm. With jam you can pronounce. Not the stuff the other lot sells, in the tub that says 'spread-style'.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: He's right about the jam. Put your best berries in it, dear. It's the only real way to argue with a corporation.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: And if you're hiring: I'm very good at shouting 'fresh!' across a harbor. It's my one skill. Other than fish.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman with a clipboard, a headband and an expression of controlled panic walks straight into the stall. She apologizes to the stall.

lines.speaker: juno
lines.text: Juno! I run the Harbor Festival. Three hundred people, one stage, a brass band that only knows one song, and no catering.

lines.speaker: juno
lines.text: That's where you come in. Tarts, scones, a showpiece cake for the mayor's photo. I'll pay, I promise. In money, not exposure.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Say yes, dear. A festival is only a very large party, and we know how to throw those.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Juno ticks something off her clipboard so hard the pen goes through the paper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The market bell rings for the first time in years. The sound rolls across the water, and doors start opening all along the quay.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fruit seller drags out her barrow. The net-mender stops mending. The seagull, Gerald, retires to a bin to supervise.

lines.speaker: juno
lines.text: That's the sound! That's the festival sound! Somebody write that down. No, don't. I'll remember it. I will not remember it. Write it down.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Nothing wakes up a harbor like a bell and the smell of fresh scones, dear. We've only just begun.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere out beyond the breakwater, a very large orange tent is being unpacked. Nobody has told Juno yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tucked behind the loose brick under the till, wrapped in waxed paper, a third page of Grandma's recipe book. The ink has barely faded.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Fruit tarts, as I made them for my first Harbor Festival. Crisp pastry, good custard, and the fruit tipped on while it's still warm.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: There's a note at the bottom. 'If it sags, nobody has to know. Put more fruit on it.' That is the best baking advice I ever gave.

lines.speaker: marisol
lines.text: The captain approves of this page. The captain has been waiting six years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The page smells faintly of cinnamon and salt. The recipe book feels, for the first time, nearly whole.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lanterns on every mast. Bunting on every rope. The brass band plays its one song with enormous confidence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three hundred people queue at your stall. Some of them have brought their own plates, which Grandma would have approved of.

lines.speaker: juno
lines.text: It's working! It's actually working! Someone take my clipboard before I frame it!

lines.speaker: pell
lines.text: FRESH! FRESH SCONES! Also fish! But mostly scones!

lines.speaker: marisol
lines.text: The ferry will wait. Let it wait. The captain would like a second tart.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Look at them all, dear. Every plate is a little 'thank you'. Hold on to this feeling. Bake from it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Out past the breakwater, the orange tent's banner has begun, very quietly, to flap in the wrong direction.
